_description: Structured environmental reference layer. Each band converts a raw measurement into an interpretable class used by the reasoning engine. Bands are inclusive of 'min' and exclusive of 'max'.
_note_on_sources: Thresholds follow widely used agronomic and soil-survey conventions (FAO Guidelines for Soil Description / World Reference Base pH classes; FAO-ITPS Status of the World's Soil Resources for SOC degradation context; UNEP aridity index classes as used in IPCC SRCCL Chapter 3). They are interpretive bands, not measurements.

soil_ph.reference: FAO Guidelines for Soil Description, 4th ed. (2006), soil reaction classes

bands.interpretation: Extreme acidity; aluminium and manganese toxicity almost certain.
Severe aluminium toxicity, phosphorus strongly fixed, rhizobia inhibited.
Aluminium becomes soluble, phosphorus availability falls, legume nodulation impaired.
Slightly sub-optimal for most crops but workable; micronutrients well available.
Optimal range for nutrient availability and microbial activity.
Iron, zinc and phosphorus availability declining; possible carbonate soils.
Probable sodicity; structural degradation and poor infiltration likely.

soil_organic_carbon.reference: Common agronomic interpretation bands for topsoil SOC; the 2% threshold is widely cited as a soil-quality warning level, and FAO-ITPS identifies SOC loss as a principal global soil degradation process.

bands.interpretation: Severely depleted; aggregate stability, water holding capacity and microbial habitat all compromised.
Depleted topsoil typical of long-term intensive tillage with residue removal.
Below the commonly cited 2% soil-quality warning level; structure and nutrient cycling impaired.
Functional range for most arable soils.
Well-supplied; strong aggregate stability and biological activity.
Organic or peaty soil, or long-term grassland/forest topsoil.

soil_moisture.reference: Volumetric water content bands, interpreted relative to typical medium-textured soil field capacity (~25-35% VWC).

bands.interpretation: At or below wilting point for most textures; biological activity largely suspended.
Plant water stress likely during the growing season.
Near field capacity for medium-textured soils.
Above field capacity; intermittent anaerobic conditions possible.
Waterlogged; denitrification and root anoxia likely.

rainfall.reference: Aridity bands aligned with the UNEP aridity classification used in IPCC SRCCL Chapter 3 (hyper-arid, arid, semi-arid, dry sub-humid drylands).

bands.interpretation: Desert; rainfed cropping not viable.
Arid; rainfed cropping highly marginal, water is the binding constraint.
Semi-arid; rainfed cropping possible but drought risk dominates management.
Dry sub-humid; moisture limiting in some seasons.
Humid; leaching and erosion are more likely constraints than drought.
Very high rainfall; nutrient leaching and acidification risk.

temperature.reference: Mean annual air temperature bands used to set decomposition-rate and thermal-stress expectations.

bands.interpretation: Decomposition strongly temperature-limited; organic matter accumulates.
Moderate decomposition; organic matter gains are relatively easy to retain.
Balanced decomposition and production.
Rapid mineralisation; organic carbon gains require sustained inputs.
Very rapid mineralisation and high evaporative demand; carbon gains hard to hold without shade or residue cover.

species_richness.reference: Qualitative bands. Absolute richness is only interpretable against a local reference site, so the system treats these as relative classes and says so.

bands.interpretation: Depauperate; typical of intensive monoculture with no non-crop habitat.
Impoverished relative to most managed landscapes.
Typical of mixed farmland with some semi-natural elements.
Diverse; substantial semi-natural habitat present.
Exceptional richness; likely includes near-natural habitat.

habitat_diversity.unit: distinct habitat patch types on or adjacent to the holding
habitat_diversity.reference: Counts of distinct habitat types. Landscape ecology evidence indicates biodiversity benefits of semi-natural vegetation strengthen once it exceeds roughly 10-20% of the landscape.

bands.interpretation: Effectively a single habitat type; no refugia or complementary resources.
Few habitat types; limited resource continuity through the season.
Several habitat types; some structural complexity.
Structurally complex mosaic supporting varied life-history requirements.

pollution.reference: Severity classes covering agrochemical, nutrient and industrial pressure.

class_interpretation.none: No reported chemical or nutrient pressure.
class_interpretation.low: Limited input use; unlikely to be the dominant biodiversity constraint.
class_interpretation.moderate: Routine agrochemical or nutrient loading; plausible suppression of invertebrate and soil fauna.
class_interpretation.high: Heavy chemical or nutrient loading; a likely primary driver of biodiversity loss that will cap gains from habitat measures.
class_interpretation.severe: Severe contamination; remediation is a precondition for any habitat intervention to work.

deforestation.unit: qualitative severity or % tree cover loss
deforestation.reference: Severity classes for recent tree/woody cover loss on or around the holding.

bands.interpretation: No meaningful recent woody cover loss.
Minor woody cover loss.
Substantial loss; connectivity beginning to break down.
Severe loss; habitat patches likely isolated.
Near-complete clearance; recolonisation sources probably absent.

land_use.unit: categorical land use / land cover class
land_use.reference: Simplified classes mapped to IPCC land-use categories (cropland, grassland, forest land, wetlands, settlements, other land) as used in national greenhouse gas inventories.

monoculture_cropland.interpretation: Single annual crop; minimal structural or temporal habitat heterogeneity.

rotational_cropland.interpretation: Rotated annual crops; some temporal diversity but little structural habitat.

mixed_cropland.interpretation: Multiple crops with some non-crop features.

agroforestry.interpretation: Trees integrated with crops; vertically structured habitat.

orchard_plantation.interpretation: Perennial woody crop, often with bare or mown understorey.

grazing_land.interpretation: Pasture or rangeland; condition depends heavily on stocking rate.

degraded_land.interpretation: Bare or eroded land with little vegetation cover.

fallow.interpretation: Rested cropland; successional vegetation may be present.

climate_zone.reference: Derived from rainfall class when not supplied directly.
